notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "Additional Institutions with a Presence in Maine" is an h5 with no h4 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "The University of Maine System" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Maine Community College System" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 3 sub-headings are plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.
